extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: LAMBADA (LAnguage Modeling Broadened to Account for Discourse Aspects) is a dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task. It consists of narrative passages where human subjects are able to guess the target last word if exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.
extraction.creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández
extraction.citeAs: Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, pages 1525–1534, Berlin, Germany, August 7-12, 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Passages composed of a context (minimum complete sentences before target containing at least 50 tokens, averaging 4.6 sentences) and a target sentence were extracted from unpublished novels in the Book Corpus. Candidate passages were filtered using four language models to remove easy cases, and then normed by human subjects via a three-step crowdsourcing process to select only passages where the target word can be predicted given the whole passage but not given the target sentence alone.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The Book Corpus (Zhu et al., 2015), containing unpublished novels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material using a stop word list; exclusion of passages where the target word had a probability >= 0.00175 according to any of four automated language models; splitting novels randomly into disjoint partitions for training, development, and testing.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdsourced human evaluation in three steps: (1) one subject guessed the target word given the whole passage; if correct, (2) a second subject guessed based on the whole passage; if correct, (3) up to 10 subjects attempted to guess the word based only on the target sentence (with 3 guesses per sentence) until guessed or all 10 failed. Passages were included only if both broad-context subjects guessed correctly and none of the sentence-only subjects succeeded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A strict hit-or-miss approach was used: two consecutive subjects were required to exactly match the target word in the broad-context condition, and no subject (out of ten, with three guesses each) could provide it based on local context alone.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Two successful broad-context guesses, and up to ten unsuccessful sentence-only annotators (each allowed 3 guesses).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: A pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN) (Mikolov et al., 2011) and three models trained on the Book Corpus (a standard 4-gram model, a RNN, and a feed-forward model) used to filter candidate passages.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Proper nouns are heavily over-represented (48% of target words) and common nouns account for 37%, while verbs, adjectives, and adverbs are rare. More than 80% of LAMBADA passages include the target word in the context. Passages contain direct speech significantly more often than the input source text (71% vs. 61%).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Constructed such that standard language models are bound to fail by design due to filtering. The strict hit-or-miss exact matching criterion excludes plausible synonyms or alternative continuations. Verbs, adjectives, and adverbs are under-represented because they are either easily guessable from local context or hard to guess in both contexts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluating computational language models on text understanding and long-distance discourse context tracking; development data can be used for fine-tuning models.
